symptom: The redirects administration reports about 404 legacy URLs as HTTP 410 and labels the whole group as removed without replacement.
expected_behavior: Every legacy URL is classified from current evidence: direct 301 to an equivalent live page, a dedicated approved search page when the legacy URL represents durable search intent, or 410 only when no equivalent content or active entity exists.
environment: VII cumulative candidate and live vii.spaplus.co, checked 2026-11-14 Asia/Jerusalem.

steps: Read the bundled legacy redirect inventory and count the gone set.
Classify gone paths by URL family.
Compare every gone path source identity against the current live catalog API for vacations, events, rooms and spa.
Request each exact source path and candidate target from production without following redirects.
reproduction.evidence: The bundled inventory has 405 gone paths: 375 root-level place paths and 30 event/place paths, with zero legacy /s search paths. The live runtime catalog contains 16 exact source-URL matches. Two currently return 410 while their exact targets return 200: /caves_view -> /business?id=vacation-21 and /events/loft_54 -> /events/place/event-2320.

observations.observation: The 410 group is not a missing search-page queue.
observations.evidence: All 405 bundled gone URLs are place-detail style paths; none starts with /s. The legacy search-page inventory separately maps 2362 search URLs to approved canonical pages.

observations.observation: The bundled gone inventory is older than the active runtime catalog for at least two public entities.
observations.evidence: The live catalog reports vacation-21 for /caves_view and event-2320 for /events/loft_54; both target pages return HTTP 200 while the old paths return HTTP 410.

observations.observation: A catalog summary alone is insufficient to create a redirect.
observations.evidence: Several runtime summary identities currently have detail targets returning HTTP 404. Redirecting those paths would create bad 301 destinations.

hypotheses.mechanism: Every reported 410 is genuinely obsolete and has no equivalent destination.
hypotheses.prediction: No gone source path has an exact current catalog identity with a live 200 detail page.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Join gone paths to current live sourceUrl identities and verify candidate destinations.
hypotheses.result: Rejected. Two exact current identities have live 200 destinations.

hypotheses.mechanism: The static gone classification was not reconciled against the newer accepted runtime catalog, so revived or restored businesses remained 410.
hypotheses.prediction: Some gone paths exactly match live current sourceUrl values and have valid direct destination pages.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Compare all gone identities to the live four-world catalog and test both old and new URLs.
hypotheses.result: Supported for /caves_view and /events/loft_54. Each old URL returns 410 and each exact current detail page returns 200.

hypotheses.mechanism: The count mainly consists of legacy search intents for which new search pages were never created.
hypotheses.prediction: A material share of gone paths uses the legacy /s search family.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Classify every gone path by route family.
hypotheses.result: Rejected. Zero of the 405 bundled gone paths belongs to /s; search-page migration is a separate 2362-URL inventory.

fix.change: Reconcile 410 classifications against the accepted live catalog before release. Automatically propose only exact source-identity matches whose detail target returns 200; route durable search intent to the approved page workflow; keep uncertain or removed entities in a review queue rather than claiming they are definitively removed without replacement.
fix.evidence: The method identifies two safe immediate 301 corrections and refuses several tempting but invalid targets that currently return 404.

regression_checks.evidence: The gone set contains zero /s paths; 2362 managed search redirects remain in their dedicated inventory.
Both proposed direct targets return HTTP 200 and share the exact sourceUrl identity with their legacy paths.
Candidate matches whose detail targets return 404 were not approved for redirect.

remaining_unknowns: The other roughly 402 managed 410 records still require evidence-based review against current catalog, historic content and search demand; they cannot be declared correct or wrong from the count alone.
The screenshot count differs from the 405 bundled baseline because managed database overrides are merged at runtime.
authorization_boundary: Read-only diagnosis only. No redirect, page creation, CMS approval or production publication was performed.
